## Research Brief: H-1B Visa “Cumulative Workers” Graph Is Misleading

### What the Post Claims
A post by **Donald J Trump Posts TruthSocial** (an independent outlet not affiliated with President Trump) shares a video from LayoffHedge.com titled “H-1B Visa Workers into the United States.” The video shows cumulative counts labeled “CUMULATIVE H-1B WORKERS”: 812,775 in 2016, 5,152,824 in 2023, and 6,932,647 projected for 2025. It also breaks down country-of-origin shares, with India at 74.2%. The implication is that the H-1B program has admitted nearly 7 million foreign workers.

### What the Search Results Actually Show
The video is fundamentally misleading because it conflates **Labor Condition Application (LCA) filings** with unique H-1B visa workers. The LayoffHedge website itself labels its data as “6.9M LCA filings, FY2015 to FY2026” – not unique workers. Each H-1B worker generates multiple LCAs over time: one for an initial petition, and additional LCAs for extensions, changes of employer, or amendments. The U.S. Department of Labor’s Office of Foreign Labor Certification (OFLC) publicly discloses LCA data, and the cumulative 6.9 million figure refers to the total number of LCA case filings, not individual visa holders (see: [DOL Performance Data](https://www.dol.gov/agencies/eta/foreign-labor/performance) and [LayoffHedge’s own explantion](https://layoffhedge.com/h1b)).

By contrast, the actual annual cap on new H-1B visas is **85,000 per fiscal year** (65,000 regular cap plus 20,000 for U.S. advanced degree holders). For example, in FY 2026 only 85,000 new cap-subject petitions were selected from 343,981 registrations, a 65% rejection rate ([Forbes, May 15, 2025](https://www.forbes.com/sites/stuartanderson/2025/05/15/h-1b-visa-cap-results-65-rejected-immigration-fees-prompt-decline/)). Over the 11 years from 2015 to 2025, the maximum number of new H-1B visas (initial approvals) would be roughly 935,000 (85,000 × 11) – far below the 6.9 million claimed. Even counting renewals and changes of status, the total number of unique H-1B workers present at any one time is estimated at around 500,000 to 600,000, not millions. The U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) H-1B Employer Data Hub provides data on petitions, but not cumulative unique workers ([USCIS H-1B Employer Data Hub](https://www.uscis.gov/tools/reports-and-studies/h-1b-employer-data-hub)).

The video’s country shares are roughly accurate: India accounted for **72.3%** of H-1B visas issued from October 2022 to September 2023 ([Business Standard, Feb 7, 2025](https://www.business-standard.com/india-news/indians-received-72-of-all-h-1b-visas-issued-from-oct-2022-sept-2023-govt-125020700003_1.html)), and **71%** in FY 2024 ([Statista, Sep 23, 2025](https://www.statista.com/chart/9008/h1b-recipients-by-country-of-birth/)). However, that does not change the fact that the “cumulative workers” number is orders of magnitude too high.

### What Is Actually True?
The correct interpretation is that the U.S. Department of Labor has processed **6.9 million LCA filings** between FY 2015 and FY 2026 – not 6.9 million H-1B workers. Each LCA is a required step for an employer before filing a petition for a new H-1B, an extension, or a change of employer. The number of unique H-1B visa holders is far smaller, capped by law at 85,000 new entries per year plus rollover from prior years. ## Research Brief: Cruise Ship Sewage Video Fact Check

**Post Analysis**  
On April 25, 2026, Japanese X user 358ちゃん (@358chan, 229,845 followers) posted a video showing large pipes discharging dark brown liquid from ships into the ocean, with the caption “クルーズ船などの汚水処理システムが凄い！” (“Cruise ships’ sewage treatment systems are amazing!”). The video includes Japanese subtitles referencing “hundreds of tons of excrement.” The post received over 4 million impressions and generated 3,503 likes, 173 retweets, and 518 replies. Many commenters questioned the video’s authenticity, with replies such as “これAIじゃなかったっけ？” (“Wasn’t this AI?”) and pointing out visual oddities.

**Fact-Check Findings**  
Multiple independent fact-checkers have analyzed identical or nearly identical videos that have circulated since mid-2025 and concluded they are AI-generated fakes. The ITmedia article from May 20, 2025 specifically notes that a video of “a huge cruise ship releasing brown water from pipes” was being shared with claims that “Chinese ships are dumping sewage,” and that it is “AI fake” (https://www.itmedia.co.jp/aiplus/articles/2505/20/news146.html). The Japan Fact-check Center (May 20, 2025) identified clear visual anomalies: at the 10-second mark, a second, smaller cruise ship appears underneath the main ship, and human figures on a nearby boat are disproportionately large compared to the vessel (https://www.factcheckcenter.jp/fact-check/international/false-china-cruise-dumping-video/). Lead Stories published two analyses: one on May 20, 2025 confirming the video was “generated using artificial intelligence” per multiple AI detection tools (https://leadstories.com/hoax-alert/2025/05/fact-check-cruise-ships-dumping-sewage-via-pipeline-video.html), and another on May 8, 2026 specifically debunking a version claiming to show a ship named “Grand Aurelian,” noting the vessel does not exist and no reputable outlets reported such dumping (https://hoax-alert.leadstories.com/2026/05/fact-check-fake-video-shows-grand-aurelian-cruise-ship-dumping-waste-into-ocean.html). Full Fact (August 29, 2025) also concluded the video “isn’t real” and was “almost certainly generated by artificial intelligence” (https://fullfact.org/environment/cruise-ship-sewage-sea-ai-generated/). Snopes (March 24, 2025) addressed a similar still image, clarifying it did not document human waste dumping (https://www.snopes.com/fact-check/cruise-ship-dumps-waste/).

**Real-World Regulations**  
Contrary to the AI video’s depiction, modern cruise ships are subject to strict international regulations regarding sewage discharge. The Cruise Lines International Association (CLIA) states that “cruise ships do not discharge untreated sewage anywhere in the world during normal operations” (https://cruising.org/wastewater). - **No global free program:** As of January 2026, the vaccine is “primarily restricted to Russian national healthcare programs, where it is reportedly provided free to citizens” at a production cost of roughly **300,000 rubles per dose** (https://renovahospitals.com/blogs/russias-enteromix-cancer-vaccine-facts-evidence). - **Clinical trial results are preliminary:** Phase I trials began in June 2025 with 48 colorectal cancer patients; results claimed tumor reduction of 60–80% and complete elimination in early-stage patients (https://bisresearch.com/news/russia-unveils-enteromix-worlds-first-personalized-mrna-cancer-vaccine-awaits-final-approval). The tweet from @ThePersistence (December 27, 2025) asserts that in Minnesota, a registered voter can vouch for up to eight other voters on Election Day, requiring **no ID and no proof of residency**. It is true that Minnesota law allows a registered voter to vouch for up to eight other voters in their precinct on Election Day. ## Research Brief: Oregon Voter Roll Cleanup and Misrepresentation

On January 14, 2026, Elon Musk tweeted: “800k voters found to be improperly registered to vote in Oregon,” quoting a post that said “Oregon to remove up to 800,000 (!!) voters from electoral rolls.” The tweet and many replies imply that these are fraudulent or improperly registered voters, potentially indicating mass cheating. However, official sources and fact-checks confirm that these are **inactive voter registrations**—outdated records of real people who have moved or not voted recently—and that they **do not receive ballots**. The removal is a routine maintenance process mandated by federal law.

### What the Search Results Show

On January 9, 2026, Oregon Secretary of State Tobias Read announced directives to restart routine cleanup of outdated, inactive voter registration records (https://apps.oregon.gov/oregon-newsroom/OR/SOS/Posts/Post/resume-routine-cleanup-outdated-inactive-voter-registration-records-directives-tobias-read). The announcement followed a federal lawsuit filed by Judicial Watch in October 2024 alleging that Oregon violated the National Voter Registration Act (NVRA) by not removing ineligible voters. The lawsuit was settled in April 2026, with the state agreeing to share voter data and continue maintenance (https://www.judicialwatch.org/oregon-settles-lawsuit-on-voter-roll-maintenance-will-share-data/). Judicial Watch itself stated that the 800,000 inactive registrations “are kept separately from the active voter rolls and do not receive ballots” (https://www.judicialwatch.org/oregon-voter-rolls/). A fact-check by Yahoo News (January 15, 2026) quotes the Oregon Secretary of State’s office: the 800,000 people “are people who were at one time registered to vote in Oregon” and the cleanup is about “outdated” records (https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/fact-check-20-oregon-voters-095242332.html). TechDirt (January 13, 2026) explains that inactive voters are generally those whose mail-in ballots were returned as undeliverable—people who moved (https://www.techdirt.com/2026/01/13/elon-musk-plays-disinfo-telephone-how-oregons-mundane-voter-roll-cleanup-is-turned-into-false-claim-of-fake-voters/).

### Separate DMV Error – Not 800,000

Separately, in October 2024, Oregon discovered a DMV error that led to **1,920 individuals** being registered to vote without proof of eligibility (not 800,000). That error was unrelated to the inactive voter cleanup. The Oregon Secretary of State’s office later identified that only 10 of those 1,920 had a voting history (https://apps.oregon.gov/oregon-newsroom/OR/SOS/Posts/Post/dmv-potential-ineligible-voters-improper-registration-records and https://sos.oregon.gov/elections/Pages/DMV-Automatic-Voter-Registration-Error.aspx).

### Conclusion

The 800,000 “voters” are inactive registrations, not improper, fraudulent, or fake. They are real people who have moved or stopped voting; they do not receive ballots. The post’s claim that they are “improperly registered” is misleading. The actual number of improperly registered individuals from the DMV error was 1,920, not 800,000. The cleanup was a standard maintenance process prompted by a lawsuit, not evidence of widespread cheating.

## Research Brief: Tweet Claim on “Countries with the Most Africans”

A tweet from @StatsGlobe on April 16, 2026, listed countries with the largest populations of “Africans,” placing Brazil first with 112,739,744, followed by the United States (46,936,733), Colombia (15,000,000), Haiti (11,200,000), France (10,000,000), Dominican Republic (8,984,587), Cuba (7,656,042), and the United Kingdom (4,871,916). The post’s use of the term “Africans” is ambiguous and misleading, and the numbers for Brazil in particular conflate census categories in a way that overstates the population of African descent.

### Brazil: The Census Data Shows a Different Picture

The tweet’s figure for Brazil (112,739,744) appears to be the sum of Brazilians who self-identified as *preto* (Black) and *pardo* (mixed‑race) in the 2022 census. According to the official results, 20.7 million Brazilians (10.2% of the population) identified as *preto*, while 92.1 million (45.3%) identified as *pardo* ([Wikipedia: Afro-Brazilians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afro-Brazilians); [Wikipedia: Demographics of Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographics_of_Brazil)). Adding these gives 112.8 million, matching the tweet’s number. However, the *pardo* category includes people of mixed indigenous, European, and African ancestry, not solely African descent. A 2024 survey found that only 40% of *pardos* consider themselves Black ([Wikipedia: Afro-Brazilians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afro-Brazilians)). Therefore, the actual number of Brazilians who identify as Black or as being of African descent is much lower. The 2022 census recorded only 20.7 million self‑declared Black Brazilians, and even if all *pardos* who consider themselves Black are included, the total would be about 20.7 million + (40% × 92.1 million) ≈ 57.5 million—still far below the claimed 112.7 million. Historically, Brazil received approximately 4 to 5 million enslaved Africans during the slave trade, and estimates of the total population of African ancestry have ranged from 65 million to 120 million ([Minority Rights Group](https://minorityrights.org/communities/afro-brazilians/); [Refworld](https://www.refworld.org/reference/countryrep/mrgi/2008/en/65186)), but the census does not classify all *pardos* as “Africans.” The tweet’s aggregation of *preto* and *pardo* as “Africans” misrepresents the data and has been criticized by commenters (e.g., user @desdenho posted the correct census breakdown).

### United States: Estimates Vary, But the Tweet’s Number Is Within Range

For the United States, the tweet claims 46,936,733. Different sources give different estimates depending on whether they count only non‑Hispanic Black alone or include multiracial and Hispanic‑identifying Black populations. The U.S. Census Bureau’s 2024 estimate for the non‑Hispanic Black alone population was 42,951,595 ([Wikipedia: African Americans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Americans)). Statista reported “nearly 47 million” Black Americans in 2024 ([Statista](https://www.statista.com/statistics/183489/population-of-the-us-by-ethnicity-since-2000/)). BlackDemographics.com gave a broader estimate of 51,629,710 for the total Black population (including multiracial and Hispanic Black) in 2024 ([BlackDemographics.com](https://blackdemographics.com/)). The tweet’s figure aligns closely with Statista’s “nearly 47 million,” but it is below the broader estimate. It is not the only authoritative number.
